hooks._comment: ONE command: jq parses the payload once and work.mjs gets the path as --file. This comment used to say the old two-entry form failed because hooks on one event share a single stdin. That is false: each matching hook gets its own full copy (measured 2026-09-10 on Claude Code 2.1.268, and the docs at https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks say only that input arrives on stdin and all matching hooks run in parallel). The record's real blind spots: it fires only on the Edit and Write TOOLS, so a file rewritten from Bash (sed, a node or python script) is never recorded; and settings are read at launch, so a session started before this hook existed has none. Record BEFORE the syntax check: PostToolUse runs after the write, so the edit happened whether or not it parses, and `exit 2` must stay the last word.
hooks.command: f=$(jq -r '.tool_input.file_path // empty'); W="$(git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir 2>/dev/null)/../scripts/work.mjs"; [ -f "$W" ] || W="$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/scripts/work.mjs"; [ -f "$W" ] || W="./scripts/work.mjs"; [ -f "$W" ] && node "$W" touch --file "$f" --cwd "$PWD"; case "$f" in */node_modules/*) ;; *.js|*.mjs|*.cjs) node --check "$f" || exit 2;; esac; true

W="$(git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir 2>/dev/null)/../scripts/work.mjs"; [ -f "$W" ] || W="$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/scripts/work.mjs"; [ -f "$W" ] || W="./scripts/work.mjs"; [ -f "$W" ] && node "$W" packet --for-session; true

W="$(git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir 2>/dev/null)/../scripts/work.mjs"; [ -f "$W" ] || W="$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/scripts/work.mjs"; [ -f "$W" ] || W="./scripts/work.mjs"; [ -f "$W" ] && node "$W" snapshot; true

W="$(git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir 2>/dev/null)/../scripts/work.mjs"; [ -f "$W" ] || W="$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/scripts/work.mjs"; [ -f "$W" ] || W="./scripts/work.mjs"; [ -f "$W" ] && node "$W" snapshot; true
